title: LG Washer OE Error Code: How to Fix a Drain Problem
metaDescription: LG washer stuck on OE? It means the machine can't drain. Here's how to clear the pump filter, check the hose, and get your wash cycle finishing again.
symptom: The washer displays "OE" (or "DE" on some models), stops draining, and won't advance to spin.
partsNeeded: None for most fixes — a replacement drain pump only if the filter and hose are already clear

steps.heading: Check the drain hose for kinks
steps.body: Pull the washer out from the wall enough to see the drain hose. A kinked, crushed, or overly high drain-hose loop is a common cause of OE — the hose needs a clear, downward path with no more than about 8 feet of horizontal run.

steps.heading: Clear the drain pump filter
steps.body: Most LG front-load washers have a small access door in the bottom-left corner. Open it, place a shallow pan underneath (water will come out), and unscrew the filter cap slowly. Remove any lint, coins, or debris and check that the small impeller inside spins freely.

steps.heading: Check for a clogged or kinked inlet to the pump
steps.body: With the filter out, look and feel inside the pump housing for anything lodged in the drain path — small items like socks, bra underwires, and coins are common culprits.

steps.heading: Inspect the external drain standpipe
steps.body: If the hose and filter are clear, the clog may be further downstream in your home's drain standpipe. Detach the hose and check that water flows freely into the standpipe.

steps.heading: Reset and run a drain/spin cycle
steps.body: Reinsert the filter, reconnect the hose, and run the washer's dedicated "Drain & Spin" cycle to confirm water clears without the code returning.

whenToCallAPro: If the filter and hose are clear but the washer still won't drain, the drain pump motor itself may have failed — this requires disassembling the front of some models to access, and replacing the pump if a multimeter check confirms no continuity.
safetyWarnings: Unplug the washer before opening the pump filter door — water and electrical connections can be close together on some models.
Expect residual water (up to a few cups) when opening the filter — have towels and a shallow pan ready.
Never run the washer with the filter door open or the filter removed.
